rows: To connect with Chinese Eastern Railway.
Chinese, private. Preliminary surveys for narrow gauge.

5. Chinchou-Aigun.¹
Alternative Schemes.
a. Chinchou-Khailar (500 miles)
b. Chinchou-Taonanfu (320 ,, )
c. Harbin-Aigun. (300 ,, )
(See No. 7.)

British-American preliminary Agreement, signed January, 1910. Negotiations suspended owing to Russian and Japanese representations. c. Proposal is to build a line from Durshenshan (via Hulan and Mergen).

6. Chihli Extra-Mural Railways.
a. Peking-Jehol (130 miles)
b. Jehol-Chihfeng (140 ,, )
c. Chingchow-Chihfeng (190 ,, )
d. Kalgan-Dolonor (190 ,, )
e. Dolonor-Chihfeng (130 ,, )
7. Harbin-Mergen-Aigun-Blagoveshchensk (410 miles). Branch line: Mergen-Tsitsihar (150 miles).
Russian concession, March 28, 1916. Loan to be floated after the European War.

9. Tatungfu-Chengtu Railway.
Tatung - Taiyuan - Tungkuan - Sianfu-Hanchungfu-Chengtu.

(See "Railways Contracted for in 1913," supra.)
Loan agreement signed July, 1913, with Franco-Belgian Syndicate. Concession to include running rights over Tungkuan-Sianfu section of No. 11.
Proposal (1909) of Ministry of Communications to connect Ili with the sea via Sianfu.

a. Ili-Lanchow (1910 miles); b. Lanchou-Sianfu (350 ,, ); c. Sianfu-Tungkuan (85 ,, ); d. Tungkuan-Honanfu (150 ,, ); e. Honan-Kaifeng (140 ,, ); f. Kaifeng-Hsuchoufu (175 ,, ); g. Hsuchoufu - Tsingkiangpu (120 ,, ); h. Tsingkiangpu - Haichow (70 ,, )

A preliminary agreement with a Belgian syndicate for a loan of 250,000,000 francs was signed in October 1912, for the construction of a line from Honan to Sianfu with extensions to Haichow and Lanchow. (See A 10.) Original private company surrendered its rights to the Government.1
12. Chengting(Chihli)-Tehchou(Shantung) Connecting line between Peking-Hankow and Tientsin-Pukow Railways.
Proposal of Ministry of Communications. Surveys completed. Now included in Japanese concession. See p. 216.
13. Sinyang-Pukow Railway. (See "Railways Contracted for in 1913," supra.)
Line will start from Wu-Yi, 20 miles north of Pukow, and run via Luchow, Liuanchow, and Kuangchow. Surveys completed.
14. Hupeh Railways. Siangyang-Shasi. Siangyang-Kuanghsui. (See also supra.)
To start from a point on the Yangtze opposite Shasi, thence via Changteh, Yuanchow, and Kueiyang to Singyifu. British concession. Length of line 655 miles, of branch, Changteh to Changsha, 105 miles.
Surveys completed. Capital to be provided, half by Chinese merchants in Shantung and half by Government. Estimated cost Tls. 10,000,000 including branch line to Lungkow.
17. Kaomi-Yihsien (Shantung province). To connect Shantung Railway at Kaomi or Kiaochou with Tientsin - Pukow Railway at Yihsien via Ichoufu.
Construction provided for under Kiaochou Agreement of 1908 (German). Now included in Japanese concession. See p. 216.
Surveyed by German engineers, 1910. Yenchoufu-Tsiningchow now under construction as branch of Tientsin - Pukow Railway (q.v.).
19. Central Kiangsu Railway. Icheng - Shiherhuei - Kuachou - Yangchou - Taichoufu - Tsingkiangpu.
Surveyed 1910. To be taken over by the Government.
20. Kueilin-Chenchou (Kuangsi province). To connect with Canton-Hankow Railway at Chengchou.
Surveyed by British engineers 1909. Chinese company formed, but no funds raised.
21. Kuangsi Railway. This line would run from Canton to Wuchow, Nanning, Lungchou, and connect at Langson with the Tongking Railway system.
Sections surveyed. Preliminary survey from Wuchow to Konghow made in May, 1911.
Concession granted (1914) to La Banque Industrielle de Chine to build line from port of Yamchow, west of Pakhoi, via Nanning, Posé, Singyi to Yunnanfu, thence via Weining to Chungking.
Concession granted to the British and Chinese Corporation (1914). Line to run from Nanking via Ningkow, Hueichow, Nanchang and Pinghsiang. Branches to Wuhu, Hangchow, and Kuangtehchow.
Survey by American engineers completed February, 1911.
Pose to Kutsingfu surveyed by Chinese engineer in 1911. American engineers are reported to have surveyed the Yunnan-Kutsingfu section.
28. Swatow-Sheklun. Swatow- Puning - Hueilai - Lukfung - Waichou - Sheklun, junction with Canton-Kowloon Railway.
29. Sunning Railway Extension (see A. 16) Sunning to Yeungkong (Makyeung River).
Connecting with Canton-Hankow Railway. To be built by Provincial syndicate.
